blocks.handshake: imem: hold imem_req and the address until imem_rvalid. dmem: hold dmem_req, address, data and byte enables until dmem_rvalid. Xpulse: one-clock t_valid with t_op, t_sub, t_rs1, t_rs2; t_rdata returns in the same clock.
blocks.latency: 18.3 clocks per instruction on straight-line code and 40.3 on bench_kernel (measured, v20 RTL simulation, make run PROG=... RUNARGS=+PROFILE). After a TWAIT deadline, software resumes 10 to 17 clocks later depending on the rotation phase (make latency).

blocks.reset: Starts at RESET_PC 0x0000_0000 (flash), or at BOOT_PC 0x4000_0000 when ui_in[7] is high as reset is released.
stages: FETCH: request the instruction, wait for imem_rvalid
ALIGN: wait for the register-file phase counter to reach 0
PASS: eight clocks, phase 0..7, one nibble each
SHIFT / MEM / XP: shifts, loads and stores, Xpulse operations
PASS (second): copy mdr into rd for results known only at the end
TWAIT: parked until a deadline
HALT: after ECALL or EBREAK

cross_cutting.text: One clock domain. Every flip-flop in the design runs on the tile clock `clk`, 50 MHz target (info.yaml clock_hz). The QSPI clock SCK is made from it, at clk/2, by qspi_ctrl. There is no second clock, so there are no clock-domain crossings inside the chip.
cross_cutting.title: Clock

cross_cutting.text: `rst_n` at the pins is active low; the wrapper inverts it to `rst`, which every block samples synchronously (on the clock edge). While reset is held every uio pin is an input, so the demo board can program the flash, and ui_in[2:0] are captured as the QSPI read latency. The register file has no reset: RISC-V leaves registers undefined and the start-up code initializes what it uses. After reset, qspi_ctrl runs its six-step memory wake-up before the first fetch (99 clocks in test/tb_tour.sv).
cross_cutting.title: Reset

cross_cutting.text: The eight ui_in pins are asynchronous to `clk`. Each goes through a two-flop synchronizer in sync_capture, and GPIO_IN and the UART receiver reuse those same flip-flops. QSPI read data (sd_in) is sampled in the `clk` domain on a fixed schedule; the read latency set at reset (ui_in[2:0]) is what absorbs board and pad delay. Not analyzed here: metastability rates (MTBF), pad delay and oscillator error.
cross_cutting.title: Asynchronous inputs

cross_cutting.text: This design has no security block, no debug port, no interrupts, no CSRs and no on-chip SRAM. dbg_pc exists as a core output but nothing is connected to it.
cross_cutting.title: Not present
